author: EmuCore - Hub
title: PPSSPP preserves filesystem order in older save states
summary: The loader accounts for known filesystem additions when restoring an older save state. A test-runner correction also ensures that requested loads actually execute.
heroAlt: A silver PSP-3000 photographed by Evan-Amos; hardware context for the PPSSPP save-state article

sourceLabels.change: Fix savestate breakage related to file system mounts

blocks.text: A save state includes virtual filesystems

PPSSPP’s August 31 correction concerns virtual filesystems stored inside a save state. The loader reads these sections in the order in which the filesystems were mounted. Each section lacks a separate length for skipping unknown content. The complete startup sequence matters because launching a disc image can register filesystem mountpoints before other initialization finishes.
Keep the older sections in order

A newer emulator build can have filesystems that an older save state does not contain. Reading a section into the wrong filesystem would misinterpret subsequent data. The change records known additions in newest-first order, including flash1: and pfat0:. It skips the missing additions while retaining the order of older mounted filesystems. Unexpected count differences produce an error.
Make sure the test actually loads the state

The change also makes the test program without a graphical interface process pending save-state operations. Previously, requesting a load did not ensure that the queued operation ran. The test program now detects a failed load and reports it. This prevents a successful process exit from being mistaken for evidence that an old snapshot loaded correctly.
Known additions have a limited solution

The compatibility list handles these known added filesystem mountpoints. It cannot safely handle arbitrary renaming, removal or reordering of filesystems. Those changes require a more descriptive format. When changing emulator builds, keep normal in-game saves and an untouched copy of important save states. A snapshot’s compatibility depends on the emulator’s stored state as well as the game data.
